subject: general
question: 102 men have provisions for 30 weeks. They are joined by 68 men. How long (in weeks) will the provisions last?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In inverse proportion problems, the product of the number of men and the time (weeks) remains constant.

Total Provision = M₁ × W₁ = M₂ × W₂

New number of men = 102 + 68 = 170

⇒ 102 × 30 = 170 × W₂

⇒ W₂ = (102 × 30) ÷ 170 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18 weeks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of men (M₁) = 102

Initial number of weeks (W₁) = 30

Additional men who joined = 68

**Formula Used:**

Since the quantity of provisions is constant for any number of men, this is a case of inverse variation:

M₁ × W₁ = M₂ × W₂
